title: NIST Next-Generation Wireless Testbed and O-RAN Standards Artifacts
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
summary: NIST's ongoing project page records open-source O-RAN testbed automation software, laboratory work using a 5G Open Testbed, and multiple 2025 contributions accepted into O-RAN test and security specifications supporting 5G/6G research.
key_findings: The project targets emerging security standards and guidance for 5G/6G Open RAN and core technologies.
NIST lists an open-source automation tool for deploying 5G O-RAN testbeds and an active 5G Open Testbed.
The page identifies multiple 2025 change requests accepted or incorporated into O-RAN test and security specification artifacts.
why_it_matters: This is an implementation record for test infrastructure and standards contributions, not merely a 6G policy aspiration.
ftfn_relevance: Adds concrete software, laboratory, change-request, and incorporated-specification artifacts to the 6G lane.
Defines later evidence gates for test results, certification, interoperability, 3GPP standards, and deployment.
evidence_limits: The artifacts support next-generation wireless research but do not constitute a completed 6G standard or commercial 6G network.
Accepted contributions do not prove broad interoperability, secure multi-vendor operation, certification, or federal deployment.
